title: READ(*, *) — list-directed input is whitespace-and-comma-delimited; surprising on quoted strings
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE LOAD_TRIPLE(A, B, C)
C     READ with format '*' is list-directed. Input '1 2 3' yields
C     A=1, B=2, C=3. But '1, 2, 3' ALSO works (commas separate);
C     'NAME 2 3' fails on a CHARACTER target because LIST-directed
C     reads expect quoted strings ('NAME'). Translating to
C     'Scanner.nextInt' in Java loses the comma-separator support.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER A, B, C
      READ (*, *) A, B, C
      END
notes: List-directed I/O is much more permissive than Java/C#'s Scanner — both whitespace and commas separate tokens, and CHARACTER values can be quoted. A direct port to Scanner.nextInt() breaks on comma-separated input. The spec must capture which delimiter forms are valid.
